newsitem.title: USA: US MIDWEST DIRECT HOGS SEEN FLAT-OFF $0.50-DEALERS.
newsitem.headline: US MIDWEST DIRECT HOGS SEEN FLAT-OFF $0.50-DEALERS.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by continued adequate hog supplies and lackluster packer demand, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.

"It seemed like there were plenty of hogs around to meet demand," an Indiana dealer said of Monday's marketings. "Prices won't be much lower (on Tuesday), but they definitely won't be any higher," he said.
Hog prices on Tuesday also were seen unstable if pork demand stays sluggish and weighs on fresh pork values, some sources noted.
Fresh pork prices at midday were quoted by USDA steady for loins and $3.00 per cwt lower for bellies, in its central carlot pork report.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants were seen $57.00 to $57.50.
Buyers for one large plant which buys hogs from Iowa and southern Minnesota area said they had the hogs needed for Tuesday and were bidding $55.50 to $56.00 for hogs to be shipped Wednesday.
Top prices at Illinois, Indiana and Ohio plants were seen at a steady $57.00, sources in those areas said.
